subject: Re: ACME - PrivateLink / IP allowlist evidence and route confirmations
messages:
From: Mario Rossi <mario.rossi@acme-procurement.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: netsec@acme-procurement.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: ACME - PrivateLink / IP allowlist evidence request

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our security team needs the following items to complete evaluation for the private connectivity piece (PrivateLink / VPC peering) before we move to procurement:

1) Network diagram showing where Redwood PrivateLink endpoints will be located (region, subnet).
2) Source IP ranges (and if they are stable) we should add to our IP allowlist for outbound egress from our VPC to Redwood (or confirmation that PrivateLink removes the need for egress rules).
3) Route table entries or example screenshots that show how traffic will flow to the endpoint (we need concrete route entries to show auditors).
4) A short note on NAT/Egress behavior for calls to third-party services (e.g., telemetry, metrics) and whether any ephemeral ports are required.
5) Audit/logging evidence that shows at least a week of connection attempts from a sandbox: timestamped logs or flow records.

Can you provide a package (diagram + CSV of IPs + route screenshots + a short doc) by EOD Monday (7/19)? Our timeline is tight.

Best,
Mario
Lead Procurement Engineer
Acme Health

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Mario Rossi <mario.rossi@acme-procurement.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 12:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME - PrivateLink / IP allowlist evidence request

Hi Mario — thanks for the clear list. We'll assemble a compliance packet that covers everything you asked for. Quick notes up-front so you have context:

- PrivateLink endpoints are Regional and we create interface endpoints in a dedicated subnet inside the region you select. There is no public internet egress for traffic routed over PrivateLink to Redwood services.
- We will provide the exact ENI-level source IP ranges you should allow (these are the IPs to add to your security team’s allowlist). They are stable for the lifetime of the endpoint but may change if you change the subnet; we'll version the CSV.
- For customers who prefer VPC peering (instead of PrivateLink) we will include sample route-table entries; note peering will require explicit egress rules on your side.

Deliverables we will upload to the shared Drive by Mon 2027-07-19 EOD:
- redwood_vpc-diagram.svg (diagram of endpoint placement + routing)
- privatelink-ips.csv (IP ranges and ownership tags)
- route-table-screenshots.zip (screenshots and example Terraform snippets)
- audit-log-snapshot.txt (7 days of flow logs from sandbox)

Rishi will add technical clarifications about NAT and ephemeral ports. Laura will put together a one-page summary for your auditors.

If you need anything sooner, let me know which item to prioritize.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_vpc-diagram.svg (image/svg+xml)]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Mario Rossi <mario.rossi@acme-procurement.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME - PrivateLink / IP allowlist evidence request

Hi Mario — quick technical notes to answer #2 and #4 from your list:

1) IP ranges: attached CSV lists the primary ENI IPs and the allocated /29 blocks assigned to each PrivateLink endpoint in us-west-2 (we will provide region-specific files if you choose another region). Those IPs are stable for the endpoint lifetime. If you rely on DNS only, you can also lock to the endpoint's interface ENI IPs.

2) NAT/Egress: When using PrivateLink for control-plane/API traffic to Redwood, there is no need for public egress from your subnets to reach Redwood; traffic terminates on the interface endpoint.
   - If your application (running in your VPC) calls external 3rd-party services, that traffic follows your VPC's normal NAT/Internet Gateway path — Redwood does not proxy arbitrary outbound third-party calls.
   - Ephemeral ports: only ephemeral outbound ports (1024-65535) are used by short-lived TCP client connections originating from your hosts to external services; for PrivateLink traffic itself, standard HTTPS ports (443) are used.

3) Route table example: for PrivateLink there is no added route entry needed for traffic bound to the interface endpoint (calls are to the interface ENI). For VPC peering, we've included a sample route: destination = 10.200.0.0/22, target = pcx-xxxxxxxx (peer). See attached screenshots and Terraform snippet.

Attachments included: privatelink-ips.csv, route-table-screenshots.zip

Let me know if you need CIDR aggregation or separate records per environment.

-Rishi
Principal Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

- Can you provide a short sample of the flow logs/audit logs that show a successful connection to the interface ENI? They asked for timestamps and the forwarding interface to match the IP ranges you gave. The sandbox snapshot is fine for that.
- For the route screenshots, please also include the route table ID and a short note naming the subnets (so auditors can map to our template).

If you can add those two items by EOD today that should allow us to sign-off on the network section.

Regards,
Mario
